FRIDAY AFTERNOON: Right now, Paramount’s Ebenezer, looks healthy for a Johnny Depp non-franchise opening with $20M+ after a $7.1M Friday/previews.

That’s around where the actor’s 2015 Black Mass ($22.6M) and 2009 Public Enemies ($25.2M) began. Sure, those were R-rated movies, but a $20M beginning for any Hollywood star-driven vehicle is surely no bah-humbug. The Ti West directed movie is booked at 3,535 theaters and will hopefully be further fattened like a goose from its availability in Dolby Cinema, PLFs, 4DX and D-box.

Second belongs to the now Paramount owned Warner Bros Animation’s The Cat in the Hat at 4,003 theaters with a second Friday of $2.9M, and 3-day of $12M, -40%, for a running cume of $38.7M by Sunday.

Third is Gids’ second weekend of Godzilla Minus Zero at 3,246 which is having a steeper fall than imagined. Sources beloved it would ease -60% in weekend 2 and the movie is acting more like a popular anime pic’s second weekend hold, -74% with $8M after a second Friday in the $2.1M-$2.4M range. At that level, the ten day-cume by Sunday would be $48.5M.

Sony’s release of Prime Focus’ Ramayana: Rise of a Legend at 1,110 theaters is posting a second Friday of $1.4M, and second weekend of $5M in fourth, -44%, for a running cume of $23.6M by EOD Sunday.

No. 5 is a toss-up between three pics: A24’s fifth frame of You Can See Everything at 1,845 theaters with a 3-day of $4.5M, -46%, after a $1.45M Friday. The running cume for the Lance Oppenheimer and Nathan Fielder co-directed movie looks to land at $87.5M by Sunday.

The No. 5 spot could also belong to Sony’s Jim Caviezel action movie Ghost Soldier at 2,558 theaters is seeing $1.3M today, a 3-day of $4M, and 5-day of total of $7.1M.

Amazon MGM Studios and 87North’s action movie How to Rob a Bank is in need of a brinks truck with $2M today, which includes previews for a $4M opening at 2,810.

FRIDAY AM: The first big greenlight of Paramount’s new administration since last year’s Skydance merger, Ti West’s edgy PG-13 Ebenezer, saw $1.5M in previews that began at 2PM. The movie for some time has been primed to be Johnny Depp’s comeback at the box office as far as non-franchises go, Paramount lighting that wick back at San Diego Comic-Con with the 3x Oscar nominee’s surprise method actor appearance which brought fireworks to the confab. Ebenezer heading into the weekend hopes to make at least $20M for the weekend for a No. 1 take, and another $20M from 63 markets including Australia, Brazil, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Korea, Mexico, Spain and the United Kingdom.

We haven’t had many Christmas-themed family movies post Covid, so comps are hard. Ebenezer‘s take is under the $3.7M previews of Amazon MGM Studio’s Red One which starred Dwayne Johnson and Chris Evans (that had action elements where as Ebenezer is spooky, so a hard comp there) and it’s under the $2.2M made by Universal/Illumination’s animated The Grinch back in 2018.

Critics aren’t wild about the net $38M take of Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol at 53% Rotten. Exits last night were 4.5 stars and a 63% definite recommend on PostTrak. Note critics are never really wild about Christmas anything, i.e. Warner Bros evergreen The Polar Express (55% Rotten, which was declared a dud when it came out but grossed $329M WW), The Grinch (60% fresh), Universal’s live action Jim Carrey How the Grinch Stole Christmas (50% Rotten), Red One (29% Rotten) and even the fun and raunchy Office Christmas Party (41%).

Sony opened Wednesday the Jim Caviezel action movie Ghost Soldier about a former Green Beret who protects his Wyoming neighbors against a ruthless corporation threatening their rural community. It’s booked at 2,558 theaters and opened Wednesday with previews to $2.3M and posted another $800K yesterday for a $3.1M running cume. Those who bought tickets gave it a 90% Rotten Tomatoes audience score and 4 stars on PostTrak while critics are sorry they were taken hostage at 42% Rotten.

Amazon MGM Studios’ has the 87North action comedy How to Rob a Bank from the Fall Guy and Bullet Train director David Leitch which robbed $900K in previews that began yesterday at 4PM. The movie, which stars Nicholas Hoult and Zoë Kravitz, moved from its Labor Day weekend frame to here in order to get more people. It’s only expected to post in the single digits over Friday-Sunday. Critics felt that their time was robbed at 33% on Rotten Tomatoes. The pic cost a reported net $40M.

One concern by some is that both Ghost Soldier and How to a Rob a Bank are going after the same male audience, though Ghost Soldier is clearly older. In terms of post Covid comps, How to Rob a Bank‘s preview figure here is on par with Universal’s Renfield which grossed $900K in previews for an $8M opening.

Pic’s blurb: Bank robbers are posting their heists on social media, causing police to chase them.

Also wide this weekend at 1,206 theaters is Bleecker Street’s release of their Cannes title Victorian Psycho which is expected to do in the single digits. The Maika Monroe and Jason Isaacs movie is 75% fresh on RT.

Toho and GKids‘ Godzilla Minus Zero ended its first global week with $73.6M we hear, which is comprised of $40.5M first week in U.S./Canada and $18.6M in Japan. #3266. How to Make Sure an 'Onion' Site on the Dark Web Is Legitimate

Thankfully, Tor Browser already has a cryptography-backed feature that can verify the authenticity of an onion site, by confirming whether it has end-to-end encryption and extended validation certificates. Here's how this feature works, where it falters, as well as what other red flags you should look for.

While phishing on the dark web works as it does on the clear web, scammers have a few unique advantages due to the secretive nature of the environment. Most importantly, you can’t just glance at an onion link to tell if the site is genuine. Normal website URLs tend to be short and memorable, while onion links are 56-character strings of alphanumeric text that look mostly like gibberish.

When you try to connect, Tor Browser verifies the URL against the originating website’s cryptographic key, which is how you know nobody has hijacked the address or tampered with it midway. But since this has the unwanted effect of making domains harder to recall, scammers have a much easier time generating lookalike addresses or creating website clones.

For example, many popular websites use “vanity prefixes” to make their onion addresses more easily identifiable or to add some branding appeal. That means their 56-character onion link starts with something like “facebook,” “bbcnews,” or “ciadotgov.” But scammers can use a free tool like mkp224o to generate lookalike addresses with the same vanity prefix as the legitimate website, which gives users a false sense of security.

Of course, most dark web users don’t type addresses directly into Tor Browser; they use dark web directories like the Hidden Wiki to find useful onion sites relevant to their search. Scammers will create fake search engines or link directories to point users to their fake websites, like when the Ahmia search engine discovered that a copy of its platform was directing users to 255 cloned services back in 2015.

Of course, it’s possible to orchestrate phishing attempts that don’t involve cloning sites at all. Researchers at Freie Universität Berlin describe a sophisticated technique where attackers serve the real website through their own reverse proxy, which lets them manipulate parts of the site or log your online activity without your awareness. In 2019, ESET even found a trojanized version of Tor Browser that replaced Bitcoin addresses on websites to direct payments to hackers. So both genuine websites and your browser itself are also vulnerable to manipulation if you download or access them from an unverified source.

There are a few best practices to avoid phishing attacks when using the dark web. None of them are foolproof on their own, but together, they considerably lower the risk of ending up on a fake or manipulated website.

On the desktop version of Tor Browser, you can access an onion site using a shortened version of its URL called an Onion Name. For now, this feature only works with SecureDrop, so newsrooms can establish tip lines with addresses like mysitename.securedrop.tor.onion, which would then redirect to the 56-character original onion address. This feature is in active development, so more platforms might support it in the future.

When you load up an onion site using the Tor Browser, you’ll see an onion icon on the address bar, which confirms that your connection is end-to-end encrypted. But you can also click on the onion icon to check if the site has an Extended Validation (EV) certificate, which tells you that its authenticity has been verified by a trusted certificate authority like DigiCert. While not every legitimate onion site will have an EV certificate, famous ones like Facebook tend to.

On the other hand, if you see a caution sign next to the onion icon, that means the site is using a self-signed or expired certificate that isn’t guaranteed by a trusted authority. It may also imply that the site is being served over an insecure URL. This doesn’t definitely tell you it’s a phishing site, but it’s a red flag to watch out for nevertheless.

Don’t rely on search engines, link directories, Reddit threads, or Telegram channels too heavily on the dark web. Once you’re sure you’ve found the onion address for a genuine site, bookmark it so you can access it directly the next time you want to visit.

If you realized that you’ve been the victim of a phishing attempt, the first step is to close the browser window with the fake site and access the real onion address to reset any account passwords you may have accidentally divulged.

Also, generally try to enable two-factor authentication and PGP logins on any dark web account that supports it for added security. And if you downloaded Tor Browser from anywhere other than the official Tor Project site, uninstall it now and grab a fresh copy from the official address.

Elizabeth Holmes’ husband has recently given his first interview about You Can See Everything, claiming that he “did not give consent” to feature his full-frontal nudity in the documentary, which has sparked Oscar buzz since its premiere last month.

“Now, did I know they were filming me in the shower? Yes. But we would film 16 hours a day,” he explained on CBS Sunday Morning. “Like, all sorts of things were filmed with assurances made. Evans confessed “I love the film,” despite being made out as a villain. “I would have preferred for that not to be the case, but it’s entertainment, you know, and I didn’t get to control that edit,” he said.

“I’m deeply passionate about my family and about the work that I do,” Evans said in the interview. “But no, I am not some controlling monster who’s leveraging his wife for insert-whatever-anybody-is-saying. No, I am not those things.”

That makes it particularly versatile if you enjoy cinematic single-player games but also spend time playing competitive titles. That said, you'll need a powerful gaming PC to take full advantage of its higher refresh rates, particularly at 4K.

The 27-inch Asus ROG Strix XG27ACDNG is a QD-OLED gaming monitor designed for fast-paced action, and it is currently down to $549 from $759. Inducted this year as a solo artist, Collins previously entered the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2010 as a member of Genesis. #3258. David Tennant Teases “Very Small Part” In ‘Only Murders In The Building”, Addresses Future Of ‘Doctor Who’: “It Deserves To Run Forever”

David Tennant is in two Hulu series releasing in late 2026, Season 2 Part 2 of Disney+’s Rivals, which is now streaming, and Season 6 of Only Murders In the Building, which premieres December 8.

During an interview with Deadline breaking down this week’s eventful three-episode return of Rivals, Tennant spoke about doing the new season of Only Murders In the Building, which sees the crime-solving trio of Charles (Steve Martin), Oliver (Martin Short) and Mabel (Selena Gomez) traveling to London to solve the murder of true crime podcaster Cinda Canning (Tina Fey).

“I’m the the definition of a cameo. I think you may also call it a very small part, but it’s either a very small part or it’s a cameo, depending on how confident I’m feeling,” Tennant said. “But lovely to be part of that, and with those legends, what a treat! To go on set like that, something that’s so established, and with people who would have every right to be terribly grand and rather standoffish; to be able to delight in their company and to work opposite these people who you have admired for years, and to find them approachable and funny and great to work with, it’s a true pleasure.” Watch on Deadline

The Season 6 OMITB guest cast — a who’s who of British actors — includes three Doctor Who stars: Tennant, who played the Tenth Doctor and the Fourteenth Doctor, Jodie Whittaker, the first woman to portray the iconic Time Lord, and Peter Capaldi, who played the Twelfth Doctor. (Also recurring is Jim Broadbent, who played an alternate version of the Eleventh Doctor in the 1999 Comic Relief special Doctor Who: The Curse of Fatal Death.)

The iconic Doctor Who is going through a complete revamp, with the BBC evaluating bids for Season 16 as part of a competitive tender launched in September. The process involves a bake-off, in which producers are asked to pitch new takes that would keep the series “relevant, surprising, brave and inspiring for both long-standing fans and new audiences.”

Deadline asked Tennant, the actor probably most closely associated with the role of the Time Lord, whether he thinks the Doctor Who franchise will survive?

“It depends who gets it, doesn’t it, and what they do with it,” he said. “It’s clearly a format that has legs. It’s done all right to survive since 1963, so there’s every reason to believe that it can. I think it’s difficult for anything in the current environment, especially a show like that, which needs a bit of money behind it, and I don’t necessarily know where that will come from. I’m so outside that loop now because all the people that I do know are no longer part of it. So I guess it depends who wins the the tender.”

Deadline has revealed that Line of Duty showrunner Jed Mercurio and his Hat Trick Mercurio, STV Studios as well as likely two different BBC Studios labels are in the running, with the process still ongoing.

“I hope so,” Tennant said about Doctor Who continuing as we await the results. “I love it. It’s a true television original, and it deserves to run forever. It will in some form, the fandom will keep it alive. We’ll have to wait and see, I’m sure somebody brilliant will give it a go. So there’s no reason why not.”

Black Friday is still a couple of weeks away, with the big shopping event falling on November 27, but Amazon's early Black Friday sale is already bringing some worthwhile discounts on Soundcore's Nebula projectors. Prices start at $299 for the compact Nebula P1i and go up to $2,799 for the premium X1S 4K laser projector, with savings of up to $700 across the models we've rounded up. There's quite a bit of variety here, too, from battery-powered projectors you can take camping or move between rooms to more powerful 4K models designed for a dedicated movie-night setup.

The Soundcore Nebula P1i is down to $299 from $399, while the Nebula P1 is $699.99, down from $799. Both offer 1080p resolution and Google TV, but their speaker setups are what make them interesting. The P1i has two 10W speakers that flip out and rotate to direct sound toward your seating area, while the P1's speakers detach completely and can run wirelessly for up to 20 hours. The P1 is also brighter at 650 ANSI lumens versus the P1i's 380, though you'll need a power outlet for either projector since neither has a built-in battery.

Small enough to slip into a bag, the Nebula Capsule 3 and Capsule 3 Laser are worth considering if you want something you can easily take on trips or move around the house. The standard Capsule 3 is down to $399 from $529, saving you $130, while the Laser version is $649.99, down from $749.99. Both offer 1080p resolution, automatic image adjustments, and up to 2.5 hours of battery life, although the Laser model is a little brighter at 300 ANSI lumens compared with the standard model's 200.

Taking movie night outdoors is a little easier with a battery-powered projector, and both the Nebula Mars 3 Air and Mars 3 are designed for just that. The smaller Mars 3 Air is down to $519.99 from $599.99, offering 1080p resolution, 400 ANSI lumens of brightness, and up to 2.5 hours of playback. The larger Mars 3, now $899.99 from $999.99, steps things up with 1,000 ANSI lumens, up to five hours of battery life in Eco mode, and a more powerful 40W speaker. It also has a weather-resistant design that's useful for camping or backyard screenings, though its extra bulk might make it less convenient to carry around.

If you're ready to move beyond 1080p, the Nebula Cosmos 4K SE at $1,099.99 (originally $1,299.99) offers a more affordable way to get 4K resolution. Its hybrid LED and laser light source delivers up to 1,800 ANSI lumens, while its Dolby Vision support helps bring out more detail in compatible movies and shows. You also get Google TV and automatic image adjustments for easier setup, though it doesn't have a built-in battery, so you'll need a power outlet nearby.

At the premium end of Nebula's lineup, the X1 and newer X1S are designed for a more serious home theater setup. The X1 is down to $2,299 from $2,999, saving you $700, while the X1S is $2,799 from $3,299. Both use triple-laser technology with 4K resolution, Dolby Vision, and optical zoom, but the X1S has a considerable advantage in brightness, reaching up to 6,000 ANSI lumens compared with the X1's 3,500. That extra brightness is useful in rooms with some ambient light, but the tradeoff is louder fan noise.

#3256. Nationwide Ground Stop: Secretary Duffy Blames Router, Trump Blames Biden

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and President Donald Trump offered up two very different explanations for what caused the nationwide ground stop on Friday ... with one pointing to a faulty router, the other blaming Joe Biden.

In several TV appearances Sunday, Duffy said that a radio facility in El Dorado, Arkansas, had undergone a routine router upgrade as they transitioned from copper wires to fiber optic cable.

After spotting an issue at a radar facility in Amarillo, Texas, that had undergone the upgrade weeks ago, both facilities started pinging air traffic control communications at an abnormally high rate.

That in turn led to snowballing failures across other parts of the communications network before the order was given.

Trump's response? It's Biden's fault, of course.

Breaking his silence on the snafu, Trump took to Truth Social, writing ... "The Biden Administration was an FAA disaster. Everything they touched turned bad. Big money spent unwisely, making an old and broken system worse than when they began."

Trump -- who echoed Duffy's request for Congressional funding -- went on to praise the Federal Aviation Administration for doing a "great job."

Since Friday's ground stop ... more than 16,300 flights have been canceled through Sunday.

Duffy's remarks come after a tense moment Friday ... when he visibly shook his head and seemingly nudged DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin after Mullin blamed Duffy and the FAA's new equipment updates for overwhelming the older system.

#3252. ‘Behemoth!’s Humanity Gave Pedro Pascal “Tremendous Amount Of Hope” Amid AI Boom, Tony Gilroy Wants To “Blow Up AI Centers… At The Voting Box”

As Tony Gilroy and Pedro Pascal bring Behemoth! to the big screen, they’re championing the humanity of art amid an over-reliance on AI.

The writer/director and star of the Searchlight film, which premieres Dec. 4 in theaters, discussed the movie’s “fight for humanity” and whether artificial intelligence can replace the “incredibly humanizing element of movies.”

“The experience of shooting this movie definitely injected me with a tremendous amount of hope,” Pascal told Vanity Fair. “We weren’t making money on this movie. Nobody was. And you had the most expensive people involved in this film because of their talent and their experience. So there was just this purity of love in the work from every single department, and that was incredibly contagious.”

The Golden Globe-nominated actor added, “There are other movies this year that I think in their own way, movies that I’ve seen this year that I love so much, that fight for humanity and the storytelling. So I think that there is a sort of pushback that could be really, really thrilling as far as [creativity] is concerned, as far as politics is concerned. We want to be human beings and we want to be connected to one another and we want to tell each other’s stories and witness each other’s stories and we want to look after each other and all that shit. That’s my hope.” Watch on Deadline

For Gilroy, “people’s natural resistance to the robot takeover is clear” in both the film and music industries. “I don’t know what’s going to happen. I really don’t. The music scene out here is the coral reef of what’s happened. It’s been dying out here for the last 15 years… It’s grooving a little bit now. I think people want humans,” he explained.

“I don’t know what’s going to come back, but this is this incredibly humanizing element of movies that’s happened,” added Gilroy. “Can it be replaced by AI? Probably, quite shockingly, simply. There’s probably an emotional amplitude knob on some f—ing algorithm, but this movie is organic.”

The 2x Oscar nominee recommended we “blow up the AI centers, man,” before clarifying, “I don’t mean to blow them up. I mean blow them up at the voting box. Go and vote and blow them up.”

In Behemoth!, premiering Dec. 4 in theaters, Pascal stars as cellist Alex Serian, a former child prodigy who returns home to Los Angeles to compose film scores and reconnect with his family.

Written and directed by Gilroy, the Searchlight Pictures film also stars Olivia Wilde, Eva Victor, Will Arnett, Hank Azaria, Margarita Levieva and Matthew Lillard.

#3249. Google announces Gemini 4 Hydrogen with ‘significant leaps’ in speed, intelligence

After this week’s Carbon availability, Google today unveiled Gemini 4 Hydrogen instead of keeping the “Flash” branding. This model is billed as bringing “cutting-edge intelligence to everyone.”

Compared to Gemini 3.8 Flash (which launched in September), Hydrogen is billed as a “major standalone upgrade” with “significant leaps in both speed and intelligence.” It offers native 1 million-token input and up to 1 million output tokens. Specifically:

“Hydrogen surpasses Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level (51 vs. 50, and reaching 54 at its highest xhigh thinking setting), while often completing tasks faster than models in its class.”

In the Gemini app, Hydrogen is better at following and sticking to your tone, format, and rules, while offering clear tables and visual breakdowns. As such, “email drafts, study guides, rewrites, and documents come back ready to use on the first try.” Additionally, Hydrogen “more frequently calls the right tools (i.e., Connected Apps) and skills for the job.”

In the model picker, 4 Hydrogen is billed as providing “Everyday help.”

Free users in the Gemini app get access to Hydrogen via the “[Auto] model selection when it’s the appropriate model for the prompt.”

Google says Hydrogen significantly upgrades Search (AI Mode) by better understanding your intent:

…you can ask your question in your natural flow of thought — even if you have multiple parts to your query, hard-to-understand typos, or highly specific requests — and Search will intelligently comprehend what you’re looking for.

Responses get more visual and will feature a wider range of relevant links. Hydrogen is the default model for AI Mode and is used for “your hardest questions” in AI Overviews.

This was a nice surprise when I opened the app an hour or two ago. It seems to be noticeably better, too.

In Google Antigravity, 4 Hydrogen has an “Extra” thinking tier alongside Low, Medium, and High. Then there’s Orchestrator: “Carbon that may offload routine steps to Hydrogen. Same Carbon-level quality, fewer tokens used.”

To help make this multi-model collaboration automatic, we’re introducing Orchestrator in Google Antigravity. Rather than using a single model from start to finish, Orchestrator dynamically switches between models like Carbon and Hydrogen within the same session.

For workflows that require parallel agents, Carbon can act as the coordinator while Hydrogen can power worker and verifier agents to build and test changes simultaneously across isolated workspaces — helping teams ship complex projects faster without driving up token costs.

For developers, Hydrogen costs $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.

#3247. 10 Shows Like 'The Traitors' You Should Watch Next

Ross Johnson writes about television, film, and literature for Lifehacker. He has a degree in political science from the University of Rochester and has previously been a legal writer and editor for Thomson Reuters, for which he later traveled around India and the Middle East as an educator specializing in American English style and grammar for adults.

Ross has been an actor on stage, in commercials, and in independent films since childhood, and has written hundreds of articles and essays on genre literature and cinema for Barnes & Noble, Gizmodo, Kotaku, and Yahoo! Entertainment.Ross produces the Swan Songs film podcast and hosts The Sound of Tomorrow, a pop culture and current affairs radio show based in Rochester, New York, where he lives with his husband and dogs and supports the local arts and cinema scene. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

What started as De Verraders way back in 2021 has become a global reality phenomenon: Peacock in the U.S. hosts the American version with the sartorially supreme Alan Cumming, and also the earlier UK take as well as iterations from Australia, Canada, and New Zealand—but there are spin-offs in France, India, Germany, Ireland, Turkey, and more. Basically, throw a dart at a map and you're likely to hit a country with its own take on The Traitors. And yet! The addictive nature of reality TV means that we can't really ever get enough. In that spirit, here's more backbiting reality TV, and a couple of dramas that offer up similarly duplicitous thrills.

A reality show with a complex history as relates to The Traitors, the premise being so similar that it may well have served as an inspiration. Here, players participate in collaborative missions in order to build a prize fund. But it's not all fun and games: There's a secret double agent among the group (the mole, obviously) whose sole task is to undermine the ability of the rest of the group to earn money. Eliminations are done via quiz: The group is grilled on the information they've collected about the mole, and whoever knows the least gets the boot. Originally airing in the aughts, Netflix brought it back for a couple of seasons more recently, with the potential for more to come. Stream the most recent seasons of The Mole on Netflix.

If there were a prize for dramatic title (and set design), you could do a lot worse than this one. In this South Korean reality show, 12 celebrity contestants are challenged to build a prize pot through strategy games. Sometimes they're collaborative, sometimes entirely competitive, and sometimes a blend, but prizes come in the form of "Pieces" that can be won or lost (and that eventually combine to create their own final puzzle). Anyone who finds themselves without a single Piece is out. Pieces can be spent to buy advantages, and also traded, so the show turns on players forming alliances in order to build the prize pot and survive as long as possible. Stream The Devil's Plan on Netflix.

Here, a bunch of strangers are holed up in an apartment building, cut off from the outside world—and each other. Players can only interact via a custom app, and, thus, can portray themselves however they want, whether that means being 100% genuine (unlikely!) or creating a whole new persona. Players judge the competition based on their interactions, determining the "Influencers" who will get to decide on the eliminations. The show ran for seven seasons on Netflix, and is moving to Hulu for the forthcoming eighth. Stream The Circle on Hulu.

You show up at a fancy hotel, and someone hands you a suitcase containing one million dollars. It's yours to keep—as long as you can keep it a secret. In this one, all the contestants get a suitcase, and only one contains the money. Much as with The Traitors, the goal is to figure out who's keeping the secret, with challenges designed to help flush that person out. If the truth is discovered via a vote, that former millionaire is ousted and the money is concealed in another suitcase until the final contestants are given the opportunity to swap bags with someone who they think has the money. Easy come, easy go, I guess. Stream Million Dollar Secret on Netflix.

I'm a little more into the normies on Traitors myself, but there's no question that a big part of the appeal (for most seasons) is watching reality-show celebs go at it with cash on the line. So it is with House of Villains, a Big Brother-style competition with Joel McHale as ringmaster. The core premise is pretty simple: villains (Richard Hatch, Tom Sandoval, Jonny Fairplay, one-time Trump bestie Omarosa Newman, etc.) compete in challenges for rewards and for safety from the inevitable banishment. It's all mostly an excuse to watch some of TV's biggest personalities go for each other's jugulars. Stream House of Villains on Peacock.

This is not a reality show, but rather a drama about a reality show that may well slake your thirst for treachery while offering up consequences a bit more dramatic than the bruised egos and hurt feelings of The Traitors. Here, eight strangers are selected to compete in a game in which they're locked together in a building and sequestered on different floors each night. They earn money for each minute they last in the game, but all their provisions must be purchased with money they've won, at an extreme markup. At first, the contestants pool their resources so that everyone gets more money—until they learn that people on higher floors are getting more. Then things get nasty Stream The 8 Show on Netflix.

This one plays a bit like The Traitors in reverse: A $250,000 prize pot is, right off the bat, allocated to all 11 contestants who get to hang out in a luxurious villa. So the game isn't about winning money so much as it is about how much you'll keep and how much you're willing to share. Eliminations offer the opportunity to remove those who the others don't want to share with—though contestants don't have to actually ever vote anyone out. They can just keep their portion of the money and hang out, something that obviously does not happen. Challenges along the way force contestants to reveal embarrassing and sometimes ugly truths about themselves that may well put them on the outs with the others. There's only one season at present, though there's potential for more. Stream The Trust on Netflix.

Blending the Big Brother-esque social aspects of Traitors with Survivor's love of the great outdoors, this one drops four teams of four into the Alaskan wilderness (moving to Panama for season three). The contestants are all, by inclination, loners, but the game has only one core rule: Only a team (of at least two) can win, so while the game has the typical reality show eliminations, these wilderness enthusiasts must work together in order to take the money. In the same way that The Traitors creates a tension between competition and cooperation via its communal prize pot, Outlast sees its contestants forced to maintain relationships whether they like it or not. Stream Outlast on Netflix.

The tasks on Traitors aren't typically the most thrilling part of the show, which makes this James Bond-branded competition a solid match if you want more complicated and better developed challenges. In this one, nine teams of two visit exotic locations in each episode and compete in spy-themed activities with the ultimate goal of winning £1 million by making it to the end. It leaves out the bits where people sit around a castle strategizing, but it includes, like Traitors, a dapper Scotsman not afraid to camp it up—in this case, Brian Cox, serving as the spymaster who directs the teams in their missions. Stream 007: Road to a Million on Prime Video.

Squid Game: The Challenge would probably be a more reasonable choice for this list—given that it's a proper reality show and not a blood-chilling thriller. But I'm sticking with the original drama here since, as perfectly entertaining as that spin-off is, it feels like it misses the point. In the original (surprise smash hit) drama, 454 needy contestants are recruited for a new reality competition in which they're tasked to play rather simple children's games—with deadly consequences that are cheered on by the wealthy financiers who are willing to pay good money to watch both the poors go at each other, as people turn on each other to survive and to win the rather shockingly large prize. A bit like The Traitors if all of Alan's murder schtick were literally true. Stream Squid Game on Netflix.

#3244. Five Things I Wish I'd Known Before Getting a Foldable Phone

The iPhone Duo might be the highest profile foldable phone to date, but it’s by no means the first. Personally, I’ve had my eye on the Google variant, the Pixel 11 Pro Fold—and recently I finally took the plunge. I thought I’d done my research to know how different having a foldable phone would be, but I still had a bit to learn. Here are some of the things I wish I’ve learned along the way after making the jump to foldables.

One of the most notable aspects of the iPhone Duo is how wide its screen is, even while closed. And there’s a good reason for that: The larger screen while open has exactly the same 1.41:1 aspect ratio as the smaller screen while closed. This has a ripple effect on how every app you use looks and feels—and whether you like Apple’s approach is largely a matter of personal preference.

Compare with my Pixel 11 Pro Fold, which features an extremely tall 2.17:1 aspect ratio when closed, but a nearly square 1:04:1 aspect ratio when open. On the outer screen, apps are a little less wide than on my old phone, but there’s plenty of space for reading books or articles on the inner screen.

I like the tall, thin display personally because it feels easier to reach buttons with my thumb, and the wider display is better for reading. However, this approach can occasionally result in some odd app layouts. Not every app is designed for tablets, especially on Android, and shifting the aspect ratio between the inner and outer display sometimes means re-rendering or even restarting an app entirely to load properly.

The iPhone Duo has a more consistent aspect ratio and general feel between the inner and outer display, but it comes at the cost of a really wide phone. Neither approach is better or worse on its own, but it might be worth going to a local store to get your hands on the phone you’re thinking about before buying.

For years, the screens on most smartphones have been made of increasingly tough and scratch-resistant glass. So tough that you might not even need a screen protector anymore. On a foldable phone, that can be true of the outside display, but it’s very much not when it comes to the inner, foldable display.

Screens might be foldable, but the strong, durable glass that makes your phone so scratch-resistant isn’t. No matter what foldable phone you use, the covering on the inner display will be more flexible, and thus softer. Apple uses a nano-texture polymer film that can be replaced, but the film on most foldable phones cannot. That means if they get damaged or scratched, those marks will be there for the life of your phone.

If you (like me) haven’t considered a screen protector in a while, it might be time to try one again, at least for the inner display. It’s also worth keeping in mind how rough you plan to be with your phone. Construction sites or factories might not be the best home for a foldable phone you plan to open a lot, but an office job should be a bit safer.

Similar to the screen protector issue, cases can be more of a headache. Most rigid cases will come in two pieces, and the piece that covers the outer display can be shockingly minimal—barely more than a frame, for some of the cases I looked at. A poorly made case can be brittle or pop off more easily, so it’s more important to get a high-quality one.

If you like to use your phone case as your wallet, it’s also important to be wary of cases that aren’t specifically designed for your model of phone (and maybe some that are). A lot of wallet cases are built to unfold to reveal your phone’s screen on one side, and your cards and ID on the other. But depending on how your foldable phone unfolds, it could be awkward to reach the inner screen.

The hinge also introduces more spaces for dust and debris to get into your phone. Despite the extra moving parts and gaps, most foldable phones still offer the now-standard IP68 dust and water resistance rating. That mainly applies to what can get inside and damage the components inside your phone. It’s still possible for hair and dirt to get gummed up in any pinchable spaces, so look out for any case that might provide even more nooks for dust to collect in.

I’ve set up most of my apps how I like them by now, but when I first got my foldable phone, I had to revisit some settings I thought I was done messing with. One of the most notable examples was my ebook apps: I was previously using a single-column, medium-font layout, but it looked ridiculous on the inner display. After switching to a two-column layout, it not only felt more natural, but a lot like reading a regular book.

Similarly, there were some uses for my calendar app that got a whole lot more useful. I’ve never really been able to use anything other than either the one-day or Schedule view if I want to make out anything, but on the inner screen, I can finally look at my week at a glance. But that meant tweaking some things—like showing reminders, which fit naturally amid my events in Schedule view, but become a cluttered mess when I saw 14 different reminders to take my meds at once in the Week view.

Most apps do a decent job of automatically adjusting to different screen sizes, but I found a few outliers that I had to figure out myself. As an example, Google Docs would default to a view with extremely tiny text when I first started using it. It took me a bit to figure out that this was due to a “Print layout” toggle in the document’s settings. This is, for some reason, enabled by default when opening a document on the larger inner screen. It can take some time to learn the eccentricities of all your apps, but it’s worth poking around when you can.

I know, it sounds so obvious, right? The outer screen is the one you’ll use most often, so how could you forget about it? But when you unfold the inner screen, the outer one is still useful in some surprising ways that I hadn’t even considered until I went poking around in some of my apps.

One of the most adorable examples is the Made You Look feature in the Pixel’s Camera app. When unfolded, you can take a picture using the rear camera and see a preview like normal, while the outer screen shows silly animations to capture the attention of a baby or toddler that you want to look into the camera. Admittedly, this is an older feature, but it’s a clever one. For adults, you can also use the outer display to get a selfie preview while using the rear-facing camera.

The outer screen is also just better for some things. YouTube is one of the few apps that has a unique layout designed for a partially folded screen, with the video playing on the tilted-up portion of the screen, and video controls on the bottom portion.

However, in my experience, it was a lot nicer to watch a YouTube video by just propping up the outer screen by unfolding the phone a bit, like a kickstand. My Pixel even detected when YouTube was in full-screen mode on the outer display and would be more forgiving of unfolding the phone without switching to the inner screen. The phone anticipated I might just want to prop up the smaller screen, which I thought was a nice touch.

#3241. The Unexpected History of 'Black Friday'

Since the 1950s, Black Friday—once simply known as "the day after Thanksgiving"—has grown into a quasi-holiday in the United States marked by steep discounts, ceaseless shopping, and occasional violence. But more recently, Black Friday has also metastasized. It's not a day anymore. It's a week, a month, a veritable state of mind. (Speaking of which, check out Lifehacker's Black Friday coverage. We got all the deals, baby!)

While pre-dawn trips to the mall are waning as online shopping grows, in-person shopping on Black Friday is still a big deal in the U.S.—it’s estimated that around 80 million Americans visited a brick-and-mortar store on Black Friday in 2025. But how did Black Friday come about, and what does it all mean?

“Black Friday” in the United States originally referred to the start of the Panic of 1869, when the collapse of the price of gold devastated the national economy. “Black Friday” as a description of the day after Thanksgiving dates back to 1951; the term first appeared in the journal Factory Management and Maintenance, where it referred to the number of employees who skipped work on the day after Thanksgiving. Around the same time, the police in Philadelphia and Rochester started informally using “Black Friday” to describe the traffic and crowds that appeared in their cities as shoppers hit the stores on the day after Thanksgiving. The phrase gradually caught on. It was picked up by national press in 1975 when the New York Times used "Black Friday" specifically to describe the day after Thanksgiving and the shopping and sales it brings.

But even before it had a name, Black Friday was a thing. The day after Thanksgiving has been known by merchants as the start of the shopping season since the late 1800s. By the early 20th century, retailers sponsored Thanksgiving Day parades that traditionally ended with an appearance by Santa Claus, as if to say, “Now it’s time to shop for Christmas.” By unspoken agreement among retailers, Christmas-themed advertisements rarely appeared before Thanksgiving in our grandparents’ day. This informal bargain obviously no longer applies.

Referring to a day as “black” traditionally denotes a period of calamity or tragedy, leading some to suggest different names for the day. In the early 1960s, Philadelphia merchants suggested “Big Friday,” a name which did not catch on, leaving retailers with the weak explanation that the “black” in Black Friday refers to the black ink denoting profits in a ledger. Oft-repeated lore suggests that retailers are "in the red" all year, and only start making an annual profit at the end of the year, but big retail chains generally make money all year long.

A more modern issue with the name is that Black Friday sales now last for days or even weeks, beginning in early to mid-November and bleeding over into the following Saturday, Sunday, “Cyber Monday,” Tuesday, and beyond, leading people to say things like, “Do you want to go Black Friday shopping this Sunday?” So far, alternative names like “Five-Day Frenzy” and “The day I get to trample someone to save $8 on a Nespresso” haven’t caught on. But here’s hoping.

Beginning around 2010, an insatiable thirst for profits led many retailers to push the start of Black Friday shopping to Thursday (aka Thanksgiving Day). Kmart opened Thanksgiving morning. Toys R Us opened that night. By 2011, Walmart was opening its doors at 10 p.m. on Thursday. The trend led to widespread backlash, with many Americans appalled that employees were forced to work on Thanksgiving or angry that consumerism was encroaching upon a holiday meant to celebrate colonialism. By 2021, most major retailers had relented and elected to remain closed on Thanksgiving.

The term “Cyber Monday” describes the boost in online retail sales on the Monday after Thanksgiving, sparked by workers returning to the office and getting right to online shopping. The term first appeared on Nov. 28, 2005, in a Shop.org press release entitled “'Cyber Monday’ Quickly Becoming One of the Biggest Online Shopping Days of the Year," which may be the most influential press release ever written. Since its early 2000s birth, Cyber Monday has become the biggest online shopping day of the year. Americans spent $14.25 billion online on Cyber Monday 2025, according to Adobe Analytics. So is Cyber Monday bigger than Black Friday? Retailers really don't care: Analysts now tend to mash everything into the category of "Black Friday–Cyber Monday" (or even "Cyber Week").

If all this naked consumerism makes you a little squeamish, you're not alone. Anti-consumerists have named the day after Thanksgiving “Buy Nothing Day,” which you can celebrate by doing charity work, cutting up your credit cards, or simply not purchasing anything. Pioneered by artist Ted Dave and popularized by Adbusters magazine, the first Buy Nothing Day was celebrated in Canada in 1992.

It’s hard to measure the success of the alternative holiday. Both online and brick-and-mortar retail sales have increased sharply since 1992, suggesting Buy Nothing Day’s effect is negligible. On the other hand, maybe big retailers are losing millions because someone on Bluesky reminded you not to shop. Sure.

Depending on how you measure it, Black Friday has resulted in between one and 17 deaths. Jdimytai Damour is the only person killed directly due to a Black Friday sale: The 34-year-old worker was trampled to death by a surging crowd at a Long Island Walmart on Black Friday in 2008. If you include car accidents, shootings, retail worker suicides, and fatal heart attacks, Black Friday’s death toll balloons to 17, with 128 reported injuries.

Black Friday violence has even inspired a horror flick: Eli Roth's 2023 holiday-themed slasher Thanksgiving opens with a hilariously brutal Black Friday riot at a big box store, setting off a chain of events that involve a lot of people being murdered by a dude in a Pilgrim mask.

I mean, yeah, of course. Critics of Black Friday point out that there are arguably better times to buy a new TV (like the week before the Super Bowl), not to mention plenty of other goods. Savings from Black Friday shopping are often illusory—big-ticket “doorbuster” items generally sell out quickly, leaving behind goods that are, by and large, priced the same as they would be at any other time of year. Some retailers even mark up products ahead of Black Friday so the discounts look bigger. If you're buying online, your browser history, location, and cart contents can tweak the prices you see on Black Friday, as they can on any other day.

Yet despite protest holidays, the unpleasantness of shopping when stores are overcrowded, and the frustration of hunting for bargains that often aren't that great to begin with, Black Friday stubbornly remains an unofficial holiday, celebrated by over 100 million Americans in one way or another. What that says about our country's relationship with capitalism is unclear, but personally, I’m going to continue my own day-after-Thanksgiving tradition of eating pie for breakfast and thinking about going for a walk, but then watching The Quick and the Dead instead. I'm not protesting anything; I just don't need the hassle.

Walmart will hold three sales between Nov. 12 and Dec. 2, as outlined in a recent press release. The sales will be both online and in-store, and will target a mix of Walmart+ members and general shoppers.

The events will take place on three different dates:

Walmart's Black Friday Deals Event 1: Nov. 12–15

Available online and in stores starting at 6 a.m. local time

Walmart+ members get six hours of early access beginning online at 12:01 a.m. ET on Nov. 12

Walmart's Black Friday Deals Event 2: Nov. 23–29

Online only: Nov. 23 starting at 12:01 a.m. ET

Online and in stores: Nov. 27 starting at 6 a.m. local time

Walmart+ members get six hours of early access online beginning Nov. 23 at 12:01 a.m. ET

Walmart's Cyber Monday Deals Event: Nov. 30-Dec. 2

Walmart's physical stores will open at 6:00 a.m. local time on Nov. 27 for their Black Friday events. Of course, they will start online earlier, so make sure to check their website as well.

No. But if you are a Walmart+ member, you'll get early access to the sale. You can sign up for a free 30-day Walmart+ subscription and cancel it afterwards or get the annual plan for $98 ($8.17/month).

In short, yes. Though they aren't quite as impactful as they once were, Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales offer discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. Whether it's a major purchase you've been saving up for or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts, especially on items like appliances and electronics. Last year's sales included categories such as tech, home improvement, and fitness.

Black Friday used to be when major retailers offered their best deals on expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. Now, however, the distinction is almost meaningless: Every major retailer offers sales on both days, which means the smart move is to know what you want, use price trackers to monitor the deals, and refer to our Black Friday coverage, where we do all the searching, curating, and price tracking for you.

#3237. Slayer’s Tom Araya Pauses Concert to Reprimand Unruly Fans: ‘Maintain Yourself’

Slayer’s concert Saturday at Los Angeles’ Kia Forum was paused mid-show so singer Tom Araya could reprimand some unruly fans in the crowd.

“The fire marshal said we’re gonna pause. We’re gonna pause until you guys get your shit and your act together,” Araya told the fans in the arena seats. “There’s no one to blame but you. You know who I’m talking about.”

The admonishment came just seven songs into Slayer’s North American tour-ending performance; after dusting off tracks like “God Send Death,” “Bloodline” and “The Antichrist” for the first time live in nearly a decade, Slayer fans apparently got too hyped, which sparked safety concerns and a five-minute cool-off.

Tom Araya had to stop the Slayer show because things were getting out of hand pic.twitter.com/ZG3dBee5B4

It was during that timeout that Araya addressed the audience. “Quiet! I just need your attention. I don’t know how many times I had this conversation when we first started playing fucking huge places, I kept telling everybody, ‘Man, you gotta fucking maintain yourself. You can’t start destroying shit, because they’ll shut this shit down,’” he said.

“Listen, if you guys wanna have fun, you have fun right down here in front of us. Do it over here where there’s nothing you can destroy except each other. When you start doing shit on the outside of the line over there, they’re gonna shut the place down.”

“The line,” as Araya suggested, was the arena seating area, where the more casual fans were likely sitting, and where moshing and body-slamming is probably unsafe.

“You guys get so fucking crazy you start hurting each other,” Araya said. “I know it’s hard to fucking contain yourself, it’s hard to fucking maintain yourself, I know that. But you have to be respectful of the people around you, especially if you’re sitting in fucking seats.”

Araya also suggested that some fans were destroying the arena, and — when it comes time to pay for the repairs — it’s the band that foots that bill.

“We’re in a time when there’s no consequences for the shit you fucking do. We need consequences. If you guys keep that shit up, we’re gonna go home, and hope you guys don’t do it next time we come,” Araya warned. SuitShop says their made-to-order model is also more sustainable than buying premade suit sets online — with SuitShop, you make exactly what you want and only what you want, ensuring there is no waste from overproduction.

Polo Ralph Lauren’s bear sweater is an iconic gift for the preppy type. There are so many options of bears to choose from, from the Tweed Bear to the Painter Bear (and even this bow tie bear seen here), making the sweater something of a collectible. Macy’s has styles and sizes for both men and women available here.

Coach’s Chelsea Shoulder Bag went viral in 2026 and for all the right reasons: its slouchy shape, supple leather construction and minimalist design make this unisex bag a fit for basically anything and anyone. Pack the bag for work, for example, or use it as your airplane personal item when traveling. A large interior capacity and a zip pocket make organization easy, while the adjustable strap lets you sling this over your shoulder or wear it as a messenger.

Sandy Liang does coquette better than anyone and the Recital bag is the perfect gift for someone who loves all things cutesy, but doesn’t want something that’s too loud or kitschy. The understated bow detailing on the strap adds just the right touch of whimsy to an otherwise minimal bag, and the structure of the bag allows for it to transition from casual to formal occasions. It’s polished enough for a night out but also playful enough to be used as a daily bag. The Recital bag can fit right into any wardrobe as a great timeless accessory from season to season.

Dior’s luxurious creme gelée is designed to adapt to every skin type to deeply hydrate, visibly plump, and reveal a more radiant complexion. Made in France and inspired by caviar beads, It’s a self-care essential that makes a showstopping upgrade for anyone who takes skincare seriously. What we like: the formula is gentle enough for all skin types, while the beautifully-designed jar makes for a great #shelfie pic.

With a burn time of approximately 90 hours, you can’t go wrong with gifting this Le Labo candle in fan-favorite scent Santal 26. This concrete candle is a limited edition (with a special black version only available on Le Labo’s official site) and will last your gift recipient throughout the cold winter season. It’s a standout display piece for your home too, whether on a table or shelf.

This soft and cozy throw blanket adds an instant touch of elegance to your space, thanks to the artist-designed lion motif framed against sophisticated grey and stripes. Woven in Scotland from extra-fine Italian merino wool, the blanket measures 56 x 69 inches in size. It’s a gift that gives rich country manor vibes or heritage equestrian. It makes a great accent to your chaise or bed too.

Ariana Grande’s Swarovski capsule collection features sparkling music-inspired motifs, hearts, and pearls, making each piece the perfect add-on to an outfit to polish your look. In other words, you’ll have everyone coming up to you to ask, “What are you wearing?”

This classic shoe from Maison Margiela, inspired by the 1970s, has stood the test of time and is a great sneaker staple for anyone’s collection. While Black and White are classic colors, a handful of fun colors like Cloud and Boero have been added to the lineup if you’re looking for a pop. For sneakerheads on your gifting list, this is an easy way to elevate their footwear game.

Scarves are a gifting staple but think beyond basic plaid this year. Crafted with an alpaca, wool and mohair blend, this scarf can be pulled out year after year while retaining incredible softness and warmth. It also comes in a few fun colorways that add a pop of color while still being simple enough to be paired with any look.

Few sports have taken off in recent years quite like F1, and this Formula 1 book from Assouline features luxe packaging and impressive photography tracing history-making moments on and off the track. The book is even scented with notes of rubber, making it a one-of-a-kind gift and an ultimate coffee table display piece.

Baies is a crowd-favorite scent from French fragrance house Diptyque and this hourglass diffuser makes a great gift because it combines form and function. It’s a stylish addition to any room and can keep your space smelling fresh and welcoming for guests, while offering an art-inspired alternative to burning a candle.

Balenciaga always finds a way to put its own stamp on luxury (pun intended), and this passport holder is no exception. A great luxury travel gift, the passport holder is also an unexpected gift for someone who is always on the go. #3231. iOS 27’s Find My app adds convenient feature I’ve long wished for

iOS 27 is packed with new features, including several for the Find My app. One upgrade to Find My—custom sharing durations—grants a feature request I’ve had for years.

Apple’s Find My app is a great way to share your location with friends or family members on either permanent or a temporary basis.

But the “temporary” option just got a very welcome upgrade in iOS 27.

That’s because you can now set up location sharing in Find My for a custom duration. Per Apple:

users [now] have more control over how they share their location with friends and family using Find My, with new options to share for a custom duration — either for a number of minutes, hours, or days — or even set a date and time for when sharing will stop. This makes it easy for users to share their location while attending an event, or for a long weekend getaway with friends and family.

Until iOS 27, you could only choose from a very limited set of “temporary” options for sharing: for one hour, or until end of day. The only other option was “indefinitely.”

The main time I find myself adding new people to share my location with, I’m either traveling or they’re visiting me. On these occasions, the “one hour” and “until end of day” options never cut it.

So of course, I have to choose “indefinitely.” Then there’s the decision after the trip ends of either continuing to let location sharing happen, or ending sharing immediately (if I remember to). And the latter option has always felt a little awkward to me. I’d much rather schedule the sharing duration upfront.

And now with iOS 27 I can. When sharing location with someone, a new ‘Custom’ duration option allows choosing an end date and time, and/or manually setting a given number of days, hours, and minutes for sharing to continue.

It’s a great change, long overdue, and works perfectly for the scenarios Apple outlined.

Have you ever wished for custom sharing durations in Find My? Let us know in the comments.

#3230. The 10 Best Tech Deals From Walmart's 2026 Black Friday and Cyber Monday Sale

The first of Walmart's three major sales for Black Friday and Cyber Monday is now live, and there are already some amazing tech deals to take advantage of. I've gathered my top ten tech products from the sale to make your life a little easier. For more, keep tabs on our Black Friday coverage, where we post the latest deals from not just Walmart, but Amazon, Best Buy, and other retailers' Black Friday deals.

Apple's latest smartwatch is the Series 12, but don't count out the Series 11. By sacrificing a few of Apple's newest features, you can save some money on the more premium version of this last-gen Apple Watch. Right now, the Titanium Series 11 GPS + cellular model is on sale for $699. That's $100 according to Walmart, but really, you're saving $50—this version of the Series 11 was $799 when it launched, but now, the Titanium Series 12 is $749.

During WWDC 26 earlier this summer, Apple announced new Siri AI upgrades with watchOS 27—but only some Apple Watches have compatibility. Luckily, the Series 11 is one of them, at least for many of them. Some other upgrades in the new OS include a dedicated Siri app, a new app grid, a new single-tap gesture, among other features. Just note that only Series 12 and Ultra 4 can run Audio Intelligence.

Bone conduction headphones are ideal for activities where it is vital to be able to hear your surroundings. They use a technology that sends audio vibrations to your inner ear while leaving your ear canals open. Shokz is one of, if not the best, brands making bone conduction headphones right now. At the high end of Shokz's offerings sit the OpenRun Pro 2, which impressed me when I tested them out for review. Amazon currently has a restored pair for $95 (originally $135.95 and $179.99 new).

Beats are a more affordable Apple alternative to AirPods, and you can often find them with substantial discounts. You can now get the Beats Solo 4 for $69 (originally $199.95) after a 50% discount. These on-ear headphones are Siri-compatible, so you don't need to use your iPhone to ask the assistant questions. They also have personalized spatial audio, which produces "3D audio" that follows the movement of your iPhone (as long as that media supports spatial audio), as well as an impressive battery life of 50 hours.

Most, if not all, TV speakers aren't great. While you have plenty of options, the quickest and least expensive way to improve your TV's audio capabilities to buy a soundbar. Compare a soundbar's size to the thin, small speakers jammed into modern TVs. The Vizio 4.1 Pro Soundbar and rear speakers come with Dolby Atmos support and cost just $79 (originally $148). They won't win any audio awards, but it's better than any built-in TV speakers, and for $79, it'll improve your experience without breaking the bank.

If you want to take things up a notch, consider this 5.1 channel sound system. Not only does it include far more channels than a single soundbar, but you're also adding a dedicated subwoofer to the mix. A subwoofer will make those thuds, explosions, and low vibrations much more pronounced than on a soundbar alone. For $149.99 (originally $249.99), you can get the ULTIMEA 5.1 surround sound system, which comes with a soundbar—replicating left, right, and center channels—two rear speakers, and a subwoofer.

I love projectors and Roku. To me, a Roku projector just makes sense, especially at $99.97 (originally $389.99). This projector is portable and has the Roku OS already installed, so it's easy to project it against a wall, ceiling, or screen, whether it's indoors or outdoors. It's easy to set up; you just need an outlet nearby and to dim or turn off the lights. If you have Bluetooth speakers, you can hook them up to create a more immersive sound.

The TCL Q51GB is a QLED Google TV that is a great value for anyone looking for size, color, and features. The 98-inch class is heavily discounted at its $898 price (originally $1,499.99). TCL makes one of the best QLEDs for the money, and their technology keeps getting better. This TV supports Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos, and if you're a gamer, you get a refresh rate of 240Hz that is automatically triggered with its Auto Game Mode feature.

Gaming monitors can get pricey fast. At $179.99 (originally $299.99), this 27-inch Samsung Odyssey G55C curved gaming monitor offers a 1440p resolution, a 1000R curve, a 165Hz refresh rate with FreeSync and G-SYNC compatibility to keep screen tearing to a minimum, and features like Samsung’s Virtual Aim Point and Contrast Enhancer. It's a solid choice for gaming, especially at this price point.

Alienware makes great gaming laptops, and the Aurora is a great option for anyone who wants to get all the essentials without spending too much. At its current $1,099 price (originally $1,999), the Alienware Aurora 16 becomes a mid-tier gaming laptop at a "budget" price. We reviewed the higher-tier Aurora 16X and were impressed with it. The Aurora 16 has a slightly slower processor, a dimmer display with half the refresh rate, a smaller battery, and a weaker graphics card, but given its price, it's great for a gamer looking for a solid gaming laptop in the $1,000 range.

Walmart has the AirPods 4 without ANC for $89 (originally $129.99). This model comes with USB-C charging (no more Lightning charging). These are powered by Apple's H2 chip, so you'll get Personalized Spatial Audio and the ability to use head gestures to tell Siri "yes" or "no" (this also works for answering or denying calls). They are rated IP54 for dust and water resistance, offer up to five hours of listening per charge (up to 30 hours with the charging case), and can handle automatic switching with your other Apple devices. You can read more about the non-ANC AirPods in PCMag's "excellent" review.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

Black Friday isn't until November 27, but Amazon's early Black Friday 2026 sale is already bringing some decent discounts on TP-Link routers, with prices starting at $44.99 and savings of up to $100. The deals cover quite a few different networking needs, from compact travel routers that let you connect multiple devices to hotel wifi to more powerful home routers designed for faster internet plans and households with lots of connected devices.

TP-Link’s Roam routers are compact enough to travel with and let you share a hotel or public internet connection across your devices through a private Wi-Fi network—and right now, Amazon has three models on sale: the Roam 6 AX1500 for $44.99 (was $59.99), the Roam 6 AX3000 for $55.98 (was $79.99), and the Roam 7 BE3600 for $87.99 (was $119.99). All three support VPN connections and multiple operating modes, with the main differences coming down to speed. The AX1500 offers up to 1.5Gbps, the AX3000 doubles that and adds a 2.5Gbps WAN port, while the Wi-Fi 7-enabled Roam 7 reaches up to 3.6Gbps.

The TP-Link Archer AX21 V5 AX1800 is down to $54.99 from $89.99, saving you $35 on an affordable Wi-Fi 6 router for everyday home use. Its dual-band connection offers combined theoretical speeds of up to 1.8Gbps, which should be sufficient for typical activities like streaming, video calls, and browsing across several devices.

For homes with faster internet plans, multiple gamers, or lots of connected devices, TP-Link's Archer BE700 and BE770 offer tri-band Wi-Fi 7, including access to the 6GHz band for compatible devices. Both support EasyMesh for extended coverage and have 10Gbps WAN ports, although the BE770 provides faster wireless speeds and more wired connectivity. As for pricing, the TP-Link Archer BE700 is down to $248 from $349.99, saving you just over $100. It offers theoretical speeds of up to 15Gbps, a 2.5Gbps LAN port, and three Gigabit LAN ports. For just $52 more, the Archer BE770 (now $299.99, was $369.99) bumps speeds up to 18Gbps and adds a dedicated 10Gbps LAN port, making it better suited to high-speed network storage and large file transfers.

The TP-Link Deco BE25 is down to $99.98 from $129.99, saving you $30 on a Wi-Fi 7 router designed to work as part of a mesh network. It offers dual-band wireless speeds of up to 5Gbps, two 2.5Gbps Ethernet ports, and AI-driven roaming that helps connected devices switch between Deco units as you move around your home.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

Apple’s MacBook Neo sent shockwaves through the computing world when it launched at an initial price of $599. As a result, competitors quickly responded with similar budget-friendly yet premium-looking laptops. Two of the main ones I’ve reviewed are the Dell XPS 13 (2026) and HP OmniBook 5, the subjects of this post.

Like Apple’s humble laptop, these notebooks have sturdy and colorful aluminum casings instead of the monotone, cheap plastic shells usually associated with budget laptops. These Windows machines also deliver strong performance for everyday tasks like web browsing and video streaming, plus bright displays and long battery life.

If you’re a Windows user looking for a MacBook Neo alternative, you can’t go wrong with either the Dell XPS 13 or HP OmniBook 5, as they're among the best budget laptops. But which one is truly right for you? Below, I’ll detail everything you need to know about these laptops to help you decide which one to get.

The HP OmniBook 5 14 impresses thanks to its lovely design, sharp OLED panel, strong performance, and astonishing battery life. Though it lacks HDR and has a so-so webcam, it’s a worthy alternative to the MacBook Neo for Windows users.

The Dell XPS 13 (2026) is a budget laptop with few compromises, thanks to its sturdy, lightweight aluminum design, sharp, vivid touchscreen display, strong performance, and long-lasting battery life. Starting at $749, it's easily one of the best budget Windows laptops right now.

13.4-inch 2.5K (2560 x 1600) InfinityEdge touch display

1x HDMI, 2x USB-C, 1x 3.5mm headphone jack

The HP OmniBook 5 and Dell XPS 13 are both relatively affordable laptops, especially as we’re still in the middle of the RAM crisis that has driven up electronics prices. That’s important to keep in mind, as one of these Windows laptops has increased in price since launch.

The Dell XPS 13 originally had a sticker price of $699. Unfortunately, the starting configuration with 8GB of RAM and 256GB of storage now costs $749. Conversely, the HP OmniBook 5 starts at $649 with the same RAM and storage. At time of writing, HP is selling this configuration for $599, or the original price of the MacBook Neo.

Even if you opt for the higher-specced OmniBook 5 with an Intel Core 5 320 chip, 8GB of RAM, 512GB of storage, and a touch display, it’ll cost $749. Basically, you’d pay the same price as the starting XPS 13, but get a laptop with better specs. Right now, the HP OmniBook 5 offers better overall value.

Like the MacBook Neo, the HP OmniBook 5 and Dell XPS 13 have ditched the cheap plastic designs of older budget laptops. Instead, both notebooks feature the sturdy aluminum chassis you’d see on more expensive machines. Their ultraportable designs also make them perfect for travel.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

At 11.69 x 7.90 x 0.50 inches and 2.2 pounds, the XPS 13 is the smallest and lightest of the laptops I’m discussing here. Like I said in my review, Dell didn’t skimp on the XPS 13’s design, as it has the premium look you’d expect from the XPS brand. It’s also the thinnest XPS laptop ever. It comes in the relatively subdued Sky and Storm colors.

The HP OmniBook 5 is the larger of the two Windows laptops, measuring 12.3 x 8.62 x 0.46 inches. Despite its larger size, it weighs only 2.5 pounds. You can get the OmniBook 5 in one of four colors: Peony Pink, Smoke Silver, Soft Honeydew, and Starlit Blue.

HP’s laptop has the edge with port selection. While both laptops have a pair of USB-C/USB3 ports, the OmniBook 5 also has an HDMI port and a 3.5mm headphone jack.

Both laptops have excellent keyboards, but the OmniBook 5 arguably has the better one, since its keyboard deck is larger and the keys have thicker keycaps and less shallow travel distance. The touchpads on both are comparable and accurately register gestures, though the OmniBook 5's is just a tad larger.

Both laptops are sleek and elegant, but the OmniBook 5 is arguably more eye-catching thanks to its bolder color options. It also has a 180-degree hinge that goes all the way back, plus more ports than the XPS 13.

Both laptops deliver sharp image quality and vivid colors. Those are the core similarities, even though these laptops use different display technologies. Not to mention different panel sizes.

The Dell XPS 13 packs a 13.4-inch 2.5K (2560 x 1600) InfinityEdge touch display, while the HP OmniBook 5 has a 14-inch (1920×1200) OLED panel. These differences make the panels a bit tricky to compare.

The XPS 13 has a smaller IPS display, but it has a higher resolution. On the other hand, the OmniBook 5 has a lower-resolution, larger OLED display. All XPS 13 configurations have touchscreens, whereas on HP's laptop you have to pay $50 more for that feature, since touch is only available on the higher-end Core 5 chip.

What do our display benchmarks show? As you can see in the table above, the Dell XPS 13 has the brighter screen for SDR and HDR content. HP’s laptop doesn’t support HDR. Of course, both are literally outshone by the MacBook Neo’s much brighter display.

Color reproduction numbers for the sRGB and DCI-P3 color gamuts are well above 100% on the HP OmniBook 5. That means colors are much more vivid on its display than on the XPS 13. That said, the latter’s numbers are closer to 100%, so colors are more naturalistic.

Both touchscreens are responsive and accurately capture gestures and taps. The laptops are pretty equal here, though the OmniBook 5's touchscreen might be easier to use since you can lay the display completely flat on your desk.

To be clear, the HP OmniBook 5 or Dell XPS 13 aren’t built for demanding tasks like editing 4K video or playing graphically intensive games. These Intel Wildcat Lake-powered machines are designed for everyday work like using Google Docs, browsing the web, and watching videos. Basically, if you’re a student or a remote worker with a lighter workload, the laptops are ideal.

I used both laptops for work, and each handled my typical workload: dozens of open Chrome tabs, light photo editing in GIMP, and the occasional YouTube video. I only experience noticeable slowdown when I have 15 or more Chrome tabs open. But that’s only when I’m really pushing things. For the basics, neither machine hindered me.

In the Geekbench 6 CPU test, both machines have comparable single-core scores, but the XPS 13 scores slightly higher in the multi-core portion. For video transcoding (HandBrake), the XPS 13 completes the task about a minute faster than the OmniBook 5. The XPS also scored better on the Blackmagic SSD test.

Aside from SSD speeds, the MacBook Neo performed better overall in our performance tests. But between the OmniBook 5 and XPS 13 specifically, Dell’s notebook has the performance edge. That said, neither these Windows laptops nor the MacBook Neo is designed for high-end gaming, as the graphics and gaming benchmarks above show.

While the Dell XPS 13 might outperform the HP OmniBook 5, the latter has a huge advantage in battery life.

In our battery life test, which involves continuous Wi-Fi web surfing with the display set to 150 nits of brightness, the OmniBook 5 ran for 19 hours and 52 minutes! While the XPS 13 lasted an impressive 14 hours and 57 minutes (for a Windows laptop), that’s still nearly 5 hours less. The MacBook Neo doesn’t come close to matching the HP’s endurance.

The HP OmniBook 5 and the Dell XPS 13 have both raised the bar for what you should expect from budget Windows laptops. They’re both great for basic work and entertainment, just like the MacBook Neo that inspired them. For most people, either will suffice.

As for which laptop is the better MacBook Neo rival, it depends on your needs. The HP OmniBook 5 comes in various colors, has a vivid OLED panel, packs more ports, and has exceptional battery life. It also currently starts at $599 (down from $649).

Conversely, the Dell XPS 13 offers better performance, a brighter display with more natural hues, and a smaller, lighter form factor. However, it has a higher asking price of $749 than the OmniBook 5.

Again, both the OmniBook 5 and Dell XPS 13 do their jobs well. But right now, HP’s notebook arguably has the edge thanks to its more striking color options, sharp OLED panel, and lower asking price. Because of that, it's the laptop I'd buy.

As Slow Horses saddles up for Season 8, Olivia Cooke recently teased that it could be a final lap around the track.

The actress, who recently reprised her role as Sid Baker for Season 6, confirmed that she will be back for the newly announced eighth season of the Apple TV+ spy thriller from creator Will Smith and based on Mick Herron’s Slough House novels.

“I am shooting the last season!” she told The Times, before clarifying “never say never” about the fate of the series. Deadline has reached out to Apple, but no official renewal decision beyond Season 8 has been announced.

Cooke added, “But I think that’s what we’ve been told and it definitely feels like we are ending. We’re all melancholy, distracted. Yesterday, I got in the make-up chair and cried. Following her three-episode arc as MI5 agent Sidonie “Sid” Baker in the first season, during which the character was seemingly killed off, Cooke noted that she wasn’t surprised to be asked back for Season 6 because the show kept “checking my availability over the years.”

“And we stayed in touch,” explained Cooke “It was like I’d never left.”

In September, a day before the Season 6 premiere of Slow Horses, which had already been renewed early for a seventh season, Apple gave the series an early Season 8 renewal as well. The eighth season will be based on the Herron novel Clown Town, the ninth in his Slough House books.

Slow Horses follows a dysfunctional team of British intelligence agents who serve in a dumping ground department of MI5 known un-affectionately as Slough House. Gary Oldman stars as Jackson Lamb, the brilliant but cantankerous leader of the spies, who end up in Slough House due to their career-ending mistakes as they frequently find themselves blundering around the smoke and mirrors of the espionage world.
